newsitem.title: THAILAND: Bangkok Bank to float $3.0 bln bonds.
newsitem.headline: Bangkok Bank to float $3.0 bln bonds.

text.p: Thailand's largest bank Bangkok Bank Plc said on Thursday it plans to float long-term bonds of up to $3.0 billion denominated in foreign currencies.
The first tranche of the bonds, worth up to $1.5 billion, will be issued in different bonds including subordinate and perpetual bonds, the bank said in a filing to the Stock Exchange of Thailand.
The bank said the subordinate bonds would have a maturity of no more than 100 years while the other type of bonds can be redeemed within 30 years.
The second tranche, also up to $1.5 billion, will be issued as ordinary bonds and subordinate bonds under the bank's medium-term note programme.
The bonds being issued through this separate tranche will carry a 30-year maturity, the bank said but did not elaborate.
Bangkok Bank's board will later work out details and conditions of the planned bond issues, it said.
